betaRuntimeParity.commonFastObservation: meanRetention=mean_g(r_g); commonFast=fast+clamp(1-meanRetention,0,1)*(raw-fast); generated biases/reliabilities are simplex-mixed with commonFast
betaRuntimeParity.contextObserver: for each group g, a_g=1-exp(-dt/decay_g); context_g+=a_g*(raw-context_g)
betaRuntimeParity.groupSlow: lead_g=clamp(1-r_g,0,1); groupSlow_g=slow+lead_g*(fast-slow); Jaw axes use Jaw group and lip axes use Lips group
betaRuntimeParity.resetSimplex: raw/viseme-fast/viseme-slow/context start at sil=1 and all other weights=0; visible residual observer poles start at 0
betaRuntimeParity.retention: r_g = sum_previous sum_current context_g[previous] * R_g[previous,current] * fast[current]

analysis.emaTrim: begin_end is applied in the original synchronized 100 Hz/audio clock before pairing after resampling.
analysis.timing: Oculus result is timestamped at DSP-buffer completion minus reported frameDelay; each EMA frame uses only the newest result already available.

hardCenterParityControl.description: The in-domain control changes only the visible speech center from exact Beta group-slow trajectories to the former hard-winner center; both use Beta common.fast observation mixing. The cross-domain row then applies the hard-center-trained emitted coefficients directly to exact-Beta heldout features, quantifying the actual former train/runtime mismatch.

limitations: The corpus supplies EMA and forced phone labels, not Unified Expressions; runtime channel calibration is a domain-transfer proxy.
A closed mouth is evidence for bilabial place, not proof of /m/: /p/ and /b/ share closure, so Reliability must gate any correction.
The hard Oculus winner and visible face cannot guarantee recovery of a phone distinction that was discarded; outputs are calibrated compatibility posteriors, never measurements.
Only causal current and observer-history features are used; there is no future-phone lookahead.

dataset.citation: Bandekar, J., Udupa, S., and Ghosh, P. K. (2024). Articulatory synthesis using representations learnt through phonetic label-aware contrastive loss. Proc. Interspeech 2024, 427-431.
dataset.sampleRateSource: Verified from processed frame counts against paired WAV duration (approximately 100 frames/s). The 62.5 Hz in Bandekar et al. section 3.4 describes a later synthesis/vocoder downsampling step, not the published processed .pt trajectory rate.
dataset.title: SPIRE EMA Corpus

training.counting: Logistic fit/evaluation use class-balanced M/NL occurrence weights. Per-winner Oculus likelihood uses unnormalized M/NL fractional occurrence counts. Eligibility Reliability uses every forced-phone occurrence in its denominator: each occurrence contributes exactly one count distributed across its hard winners. Runtime/evaluation simplex-mix both tables with exact Beta common.fast.
training.factorization: class-balanced shared visible-face log-likelihood ratio plus a Beta-common.fast mixture of Dirichlet-smoothed per-winner log P(Oculus winner|M)/P(Oculus winner|N/L)

labels.Other: every other forced-phone occurrence, including vowels, unrelated consonants, and silence

training.posteriorSemantics: positive logit is M-compatible; negative is N/L-compatible
training.reliabilitySemantics: Dirichlet-smoothed P(the M-versus-N/L hypothesis is eligible | observed hard Oculus winner), with M/N/L eligible and P/B stops plus all other forced phones ineligible
training.stopHandling: P/B stops never become N negatives; like vowels, silence, and unrelated consonants, they lower eligibility Reliability
